artworks.title: Hercules and the Dragon Ladon
artworks.description: A bronze statuette from the workshop of the Flemish-Italian Mannerist sculptor Giambologna (1529–1608), cast in the early 17th century after a design of around 1580 for the Medici court. It captures the climax of Heracles' eleventh labour: rather than the theft of the golden apples, the artist stages the hero's violent confrontation with Ladon, the immortal serpent who guarded the tree of the Hesperides. The hero strides forward in one of the torsioned, spiralling poses characteristic of Giambologna, while the dragon writhes beneath him; the smooth, highly finished bronze surface accentuates the play of muscle and movement. Walters Art Museum, Baltimore (accession 54.695); height 41.8 cm.

artworks.title: Heracles and Ladon, Guardian of the Golden Apples
artworks.description: A Roman relief plate (the decorated disc of a terracotta oil lamp) of the late imperial period, showing Heracles and the serpent Ladon coiled about the tree of the golden apples of the Hesperides. The dragon's sinuous body winds up the trunk, embodying the watchful guardian whom the hero must overcome in his eleventh labour. From the Loeb Collection, the piece is held in the Staatliche Antikensammlungen (State Collection of Antiquities) in Munich, catalogued as SL 89. It is a characteristic example of the mass-produced figural lamps through which mythological imagery, including the labours of Heracles, circulated widely across the Roman world.

artworks.title: The Garden of the Hesperides
artworks.description: Frederic Leighton's circular late masterpiece gathers the Hesperides beneath the apple tree while Ladon coils through the branches — the hundred-headed dragon as a living garland rather than a combatant. Painted around 1892, the work turns the eleventh labour's guardian into the quiet, jewelled centre of an Aesthetic garden, Ladon present as watchfulness made beautiful.

artworks.title: The Garden of the Hesperides
artworks.description: Edward Burne-Jones's Pre-Raphaelite garden of the Hesperides winds Ladon through the golden apple tree among the evening nymphs. The dragon is not slain here but dreamily present — the sleepless guardian of Gaia's wedding gift rendered as an arabesque of scales and leaves in the Burne-Jones manner.

popCulture.title: Hesperides
popCulture.description: Ladon's modern afterlife is the western garden itself — the dragon coiled under the sunset trees of the Hesperides.

popCulture.title: The Titan's Curse
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan's hundred-headed Ladon still coils round the golden apple tree — the bite that helps kill Zoë Nightshade in the Garden of the Hesperides.

popCulture.title: Draco (constellation)
popCulture.description: Ancient star-lore identifies Draco with Ladon — the slain Hesperides dragon wound among the northern stars by Zeus.

films.title: Shazam! Fury of the Gods
films.description: Sandberg's DC sequel brings Ladon onscreen as Kalypso's dragon — the Hesperides' apple-guardian unleashed on a modern city.
